correctness.rationale: Euclidean E dominates N. By symmetry, on a>=b>=0 with t=b/a the ratio N/E has one decreasing branch and one increasing branch, so its global minimum occurs at t=sqrt(2)-1 and equals c=cos(pi/8). Hence cE<=N<=E. Hilbert Ptolemy then gives C_Pt<=c^{-2}=4-2sqrt(2). With s=sqrt(2)-1, x=(-1,s), y=(s,-1), z=(-2,-2) have N(x)=N(y)=1, N(x-y)=2, N(z)=2sqrt(2), and N(x-z)=N(z-y)=1+sqrt(2), yielding ratio exactly 4-2sqrt(2). The upper and lower bounds therefore match globally.
